_purpose: OPERATOR REFERENCE ONLY. This audit is not design DNA. The owl template is the sole source of truth for layout, structure and component styling. Only brand tokens (red/white/black, logo) and business facts were carried forward.
platform: Weebly (free tier — 'Powered by Weebly' badge renders in the footer of every page)
strengths: Genuine 1968 founding date and family-ownership story stated plainly and repeatedly
License and insurance numbers published on the logo itself (C.C. 6469 / CFC057007)
Strong, memorable tagline already in market: 'CAN FIX ANYBODY'S PLUMBING'
Clear brand color: a single saturated red (#f90909) on white/black
Substantial, specific service copy — septic, drainfield, backflow, jetting, video inspection — written in real detail rather than boilerplate
Real photo of the actual shop and signage at 3029 SW 28th St
Both phone numbers (Miami and Key Biscayne) surfaced on every page
weaknesses: Unedited template placeholder text is live in production: a 'SOMEONE ONCE SAID' pull-quote reading 'If you're writing a medium or long section of text, break it up with more than one paragraph' on /why-us
An entire orphan section titled 'It's What's for Breakfast' with coffee and cookie stock icons and 'To edit, click on the text and add your own words' — visible to every visitor on /why-us
Homepage hero overlay announces 'We are working on the ADA Compliance version. Coming Soon!' — an accessibility disclaimer instead of an offer
Hero background video is a black-and-white interior of a modern living room with mountains outside the window — not Miami, not plumbing, not theirs
The contact form's own comment field is labelled 'massage' (typo for 'message'), and the word appears again as stray body text in the footer
No testimonials or reviews anywhere on the site, despite dozens of real reviews existing on Yelp and other directories
No service-area pages — Miami-Dade is named in prose but there is no page targeting Coconut Grove, Coral Gables, Key Biscayne or South Miami
No individual service pages: everything collapses into one /services list page, so no SEO surface for 'drainfield repair Miami' or 'backflow testing Miami'
Body copy repeatedly says 'over 40 years' and 'four whole decades' — stale by nearly two decades against the 1968 date
Typo 'RESIDENTIAL & COMMERTIAL' as an H2 on /residential--commercial.html
'Bay County Plumbing' — the wrong company name — appears twice on /property-maintenance.html
Several internal links point to dead legacy paths (residential_and_commercial.html, backflow_certification_request.html) and one has a four-w typo: 'wwww.bayplumbingco.com'
No structured data, no sitemap, no canonical strategy, no analytics or pixel
Contact form collects name/email/comments only — no phone field, so an emergency lead cannot be called back
/specials.html is three untitled images with no readable offer text
Layout is table-based Weebly markup; mobile rendering degrades to stacked tables

carried_forward.logo: public/logo-bay-plumbing.png (transparent PNG, red wordmark with license line)

not_carried_forward: All layout, section rhythm, table markup and component styling
The stock hero video and all decorative stock icons
